subject: Logic
title: The Liar Paradox
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Liar Paradox.

hook.text: "This statement is false." If it's true, it's false. If it's false, it's true. Round and round.

buildup.text: Epimenides the Cretan said, "All Cretans are liars." If he's telling the truth, he's lying.

discovery.text: The liar paradox shows that self-referencing statements can break classic two-valued logic.

twist.text: Logicians tried banning self-reference. But it keeps sneaking back in through language and math.

climax.text: Modern solutions include multi-valued logic and Tarski's hierarchy of truth levels.

punchline.text: Some sentences refuse to be true or false.

quiz.question: What makes the liar paradox problematic?
